welcome_title: Discover the Hidden Numerical Miracles of the Quran
welcome_subtitle: The most advanced and flexible platform for statistical and numerical analysis of the Holy Quran. Build mathematical models, discover patterns, and explore data like never before.
feature_models_desc: Apply any equation or formula you conceive. The platform dynamically calculates and highlights patterns across Surahs, Ayahs, and Words.
feature_perf_desc: All calculations run on your device directly from the data files, with no server and no database, so results appear instantly even without a connection.
feature_api_desc: Each calculation is written once and shared by the website, the desktop program and the optional API, so results always match.
tool_unified_desc: Calculate a text, then show its triangle magic square and the words matching its value
tool_jummal_desc: Jummal, Abjad, Ayqagh and their total for any text or verse
tool_tables_desc: The value of each word and the phrase total in the tables you choose
tool_wefq_desc: Study a number in the seven shapes, then build the magic square
tool_number_search_desc: Quran words whose Jummal, Abjad or Ayqagh equals the number
tool_number_study_desc: Digital root, divisors, primality, Fibonacci and decomposition tree
enter_text_f9: Enter text or press F9 to choose a verse
err_no_letters: No valid Arabic letters to calculate
err_select_table: Please select at least one table
err_execute_first: Enter a number and press Execute first
err_select_type: Please select at least one calculation type
err_number_range: Please enter a number between 1 and {{max}}
err_min_triangle: The number must be {{min}} or more
tables_empty: Nothing calculated yet. Enter a text and press Calculate.
ayat_picker_hint: Click to select, Ctrl+click for several verses, double-click or press Enter to confirm
wefq_legend: Green: no fraction, orange: needs a fraction fix, red: below the minimum
search_hint: Enter a number and press Search
ns_prime_rank_ones: Rank among primes with the same last digit
ns_tree_too_big: The tree is large ({{nodes}} nodes), so only the summary is shown
st_FLCs: Surahs starting and ending with it
st_FLVs: Verses starting and ending with it
stats_chars_desc: Occurrences of each of the 28 letters in the Quran (28-letter text)
chars_per_chapter_desc: Count of each letter in each surah. Click a column header to sort
study_char_desc: Choose a letter to see its statistics and distribution across surahs
chapter_verses_desc: Total verses {{verses}}, total words {{words}} (conjunction waw counted as a word)
symmetric_verses_desc: Choose a surah and an axis verse: the verses are placed on a circle and each verse faces its mirror on the other side of the axis (axis+1 with axis-1, and so on), with word and letter totals for each pair
circle_desc: Hover a surah to draw its symmetry line and the total verses of the pair; click to pin the line
Please Select Start Axis: Please select the axis start surah
app_name: Numerical Studies in the Holy Quran
study_chapter_desc: Choose a surah to see its details and its used and unused letters
study_verse_desc: Choose a surah, then a verse, to see its details and letters
study_range_desc: Pick where the range starts and ends (surah, verse, word, letter) to see statistics for its words, letters and values in the chosen tables
compare_ranges_desc: Pick two ranges, then compare their statistics, count words in both, and apply equations between them
range_err_reversed: The range starts after it ends
equations_hint: Write an equation with the variables of ranges A and B, e.g. A.letters / B.letters. Operators: + - * / % ^ and brackets
eq_var_letter: Count of a letter (any of the 28)
eq_variables_help: Available variables (click to insert; use B instead of A for the second range)
eq_functions_help: Functions: abs, sqrt, round, floor, ceil, min, max. Added words: A.w1, B.w1 ...
range_chart_letters: Frequency of the 28 letters in the range
math_lab_desc: Write any equation, one per line: sums, powers and roots, statistics, derivatives and integrals, matrices and number theory, with variables and functions from the Quran text
ml_editor_hint: One equation per line; lines starting with # are comments. Define variables and functions (x = 19, f(x) = x^2) and use them on later lines. Ctrl+Enter to run
ml_ref_totals: Number of surahs, verses, words and letters in the Quran
ml_ref_surah_vectors: A 114-value sequence: verses/words/letters per surah. surahVerses[2] is Al-Baqarah
ml_ref_surah_tables: Each surah's value in the five tables
ml_ref_surah_info: Revelation order per surah, and 1 for Meccan, 0 for Medinan
ml_ref_verse_vectors: A 6,236-value sequence: words, letters, values, surah and number of every verse
ml_ref_letters: Counts of the 28 letters in abjad order, and their Jummal values
ml_ref_letter_fn: Count of a letter in the Quran, or in one surah
ml_ref_word_fn: Count of an exact word, or of every word containing it
ml_ref_value_fn: Value of a text in a table: jummal, abjad, ayqagh, tabaei4, tabaei7
ml_ref_bysurah_fn: A sequence with one value per verse of a surah
ml_ref_segment_fn: A range (surah:verse:word:letter): verses, words, distinct, letters, jummal..., verseWords, verseLetters, text
ml_ref_text_fn: A verse's 28-letter text, and letters and words of a text you type
ml_ref_powers: Operators, powers and roots. bignumber keeps every digit of large numbers
ml_ref_calculus: Symbolic derivative and simplification, numeric integral and derivative, equation root, sum and product
ml_ref_statistics: Statistics and linear regression (slope, intercept, r, r2)
ml_ref_numbers: Primes, divisors, digit sum, digital root and Fibonacci
ml_approx_hint: Approximate large number. For the exact value with every digit, write bignumber(2)^64
